title: The Flower of Utah
question: Today, can Lucy John Ferrier ride into the city and come back her own?
palette: Warm high-summer palette of gold ripe wheat, red road dust and deep green pine, hard blue shadow under a clear bleached sky; the Utah valley and Salt Lake City, June 1860; American frontier, sunlight and lamplight only.

valley_rim.described: The rim of the pass above the valley of Utah at sunrise, June 1847: a bare rock shoulder falling away to a broad green valley floor, a flat silver inland sea along its far side, a chain of snow-flecked peaks beyond that, sagebrush and red dust underfoot, the sun low behind the near ridge
valley_rim.landmark: the flat silver inland sea on the valley floor
valley_rim.landmark_size: is the height of a hand
valley_rim.route: from the crest of the pass down the rock shoulder to the first grass
valley_rim.geometry: The silver inland sea lies along the TOP third of the frame at the far side of the valley. The snow-flecked peaks stand above it along the skyline. The bare rock shoulder fills the BOTTOM third and the near right corner.
valley_rim.crowd: Forty immigrants in dust-grey homespun kneel along the rock shoulder with their hats off, and beyond them twelve canvas-topped waggons stand in a line with their oxen still in the yoke.

ferrier_land.described: John Ferrier's farm on the valley floor, June 1860: a long low log house grown room by room into a rambling villa with a shingled roof and a deep porch, a rail fence running out from it, a hundred acres of ripe gold wheat beyond the fence, red pine hills behind, hard morning sunlight
ferrier_land.landmark: the log house with its deep porch
ferrier_land.route: from the porch steps out along the rail fence into the standing wheat
ferrier_land.geometry: The log house stands along the LEFT edge with its porch posts in the near ground. The rail fence runs from the bottom left corner to the centre of the frame. The gold wheat fills the middle band and the red pine hills the TOP third.
ferrier_land.crowd: Two farm hands in shirtsleeves pitch cut wheat onto a waggon at the fence line, and a yoke of oxen stands in the shafts with a boy at their heads.

high_road.described: The dusty high road into Salt Lake City on a warm June morning, 1860: a broad rutted red-dust road between low adobe walls and cottonwoods, the half-built grey stone temple standing over the roofs ahead, the Wahsatch mountains blue behind it, hanging dust gold in the low sun
high_road.landmark: the half-built grey stone temple over the roofs
high_road.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
high_road.route: from the open country at the farm end of the road in to the city outskirts
high_road.geometry: The temple stands in the TOP centre of the frame above the roofline. The rutted road runs from the bottom centre away to it. The adobe walls and cottonwoods stand along both edges.
high_road.crowd: Thirty heavily-laden pack mules file west along the left of the road with six drivers walking at their heads at a normal walking pace, a train of eight immigrant waggons rolls the other way, and four Indians lead ponies loaded with pelts along the right wall.

the_drove.described: The road at the city outskirts, packed bank to bank with a great drove of cattle on a warm June morning, 1860: long-horned bullocks shoulder to shoulder from wall to wall, a standing cloud of red dust to the height of a man, adobe walls and a rail corral on either side, hard white sun overhead
the_drove.landmark: the rail corral at the roadside
the_drove.landmark_size: is the height of a hand
the_drove.route: from the open road behind the herd through the packed drove to its far edge
the_drove.geometry: The long-horned backs of the bullocks fill the BOTTOM two thirds of the frame from edge to edge. The red dust hangs across the middle band. The adobe wall and the rail corral stand along the RIGHT edge and the TOP third is bleached sky.
the_drove.crowd: Six wild-looking herdsmen on ponies ride the flanks of the drove at a normal walking pace swinging coiled ropes, and two more sit their horses at the corral rail watching the road.

farm_parlour.described: Interior, inside the parlour of John Ferrier's log villa on a summer evening, 1860, the camera standing within the room with squared white-chinked log walls closed on all four sides and a low plank ceiling overhead: a stone hearth with a low fire burning in it, a scrubbed pine table under a hanging oil lamp, ladder-back chairs, a rag rug on the board floor, one deep window in the far wall open on the blue dusk outside; the hanging oil lamp is the light in the room and the window a pale rectangle
farm_parlour.landmark: the stone hearth with its low fire
farm_parlour.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
farm_parlour.route: from the hearth across the rag rug to the open window
farm_parlour.geometry: The stone hearth stands along the LEFT edge with the fire low in it. The pine table stands in the centre under the hanging lamp. The open window is a pale blue rectangle in the RIGHT third.
farm_parlour.crowd: Moths cross the lamp glass in ones and twos and the low fire settles in the hearth.

farm_gate.described: The gate of Ferrier's farm on a summer evening, 1860: a five-bar rail gate in the fence at the head of a beaten path, the porch of the log house behind it, gold stubble fields either side, the pine hills black against a burning orange west, long level light
farm_gate.landmark: the porch of the log house
farm_gate.landmark_size: is half the height of the frame
farm_gate.route: from the gate up the beaten path to the porch steps
farm_gate.geometry: The five-bar gate stands in the near RIGHT of the frame. The beaten path runs from the gate to the bottom left corner. The porch of the log house stands in the LEFT third and the burning orange west fills the TOP third.
farm_gate.crowd: A roan horse stands at the fence with its bridle over the rail, shifting its weight and swinging its head at the flies.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: They had crossed a continent on foot, and the last of them came over the pass at dawn.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Every man there went down on his knees when he saw the valley.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Their leader told them it was the promised land, and that it was theirs.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Among them was John Ferrier, who had walked out of the desert carrying a child.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: In three years he was comfortable, in nine he was rich, in twelve he had no equal.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The child grew up in the log house and worked beside him at everything.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The mountain air and the pines did for her what a mother would have done.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: So the bud opened into a flower, in the year her father became the richest of them.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: It was a warm June morning, and the whole valley was at work.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: The gold fever had broken out west, and the road to it ran through the city.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Through the middle of it all Lucy John Ferrier came galloping in on her father's errand.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: She was nineteen, and she had ridden that road a hundred times alone.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Strangers turned in the dust to watch her go by.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: At the edge of the city the road was stopped by a drove of cattle.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: She saw a gap and put her horse into it, and the beasts closed up behind her.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: A horn came round and struck the mustang in the flank.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: It went up, and a slip would have put her under four hundred hooves.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: You're not hurt, I hope, miss.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: I guess you are the daughter of John Ferrier.

lines.speaker: lucy_ferrier
lines.text: Hadn't you better come and ask him yourself?

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: She rode on. He sat his horse in the road and watched the dust take her.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He came to the house that night, and a great many nights after it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He had been a scout, a trapper and a miner, and he could tell it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: Her father heard him gladly. Lucy said very little at all.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: What she felt was plain enough to the one man it was meant for.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: By midsummer her heart was no longer her own, and she knew it.

lines.speaker: john_watson
lines.text: He came down the road one evening at a gallop and pulled up at the gate.

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: I am off, Lucy. Will you be ready to come when I am here again?

lines.speaker: lucy_ferrier
lines.text: And when will that be?

lines.speaker: jefferson_hope
lines.text: In two months you shall see me.
